CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right upper arm pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
39-year-old female presents with severe right upper arm pain that occurred approximately 18 hours ago during a volleyball game. Patient was spiking the ball when an opponent kicked her legs from under her, causing her to fall and land on her arm, specifically on her shoulder. Pain is rated 9 out of 10 in severity. Patient has been taking ibuprofen every 6 hours with minimal relief. Has not used ice. X-ray reveals proximal humerus fracture.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies numbness or tingling in right arm.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Gallstones.
Lumbar fusion approximately 6 years ago.

MEDICATIONS
Pepcid for gallstones.
Ibuprofen every 6 hours as needed for pain.

ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Patient able to straighten elbow without shoulder movement. Swelling and erythema noted on right shoulder. Tenderness over right shoulder. Normal pulses. Able to bend elbow. Rest of body examination normal. No numbness or tingling in right arm.

RESULTS
X-ray of right arm shows proximal humerus fracture (top of proximal humerus).

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Proximal humerus fracture of right arm. Treatment plan: immobilization with long arm cast and sling. Follow-up in 2 weeks to assess bone realignment; if inadequate realignment, surgery will be considered. Prescribed Lortab 5 mg, 1-2 tablets every 6 hours as needed for pain, quantity 20.
